target: supersede applies either way by design, but a citation only unblocks dependents when it verifiably landed. The base fell back to symbolic-ref HEAD, so on a feature branch a commit unique to that branch verified as landed and silently unblocked everything downstream
cmd: git init -q r && cd r && git config user.email t@t && git config user.name t && git commit -q --allow-empty -m base && git branch -M main && git checkout -q -b feature && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "only on feature" && SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) && mkdir -p specs && bash "$FIXTURES/tracker-gates/mkspec.sh" specs 925 queued && FACTORY_SPECS_DIR=$PWD/specs bash "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh" supersede specs/925-t.md tester "$SHA" "landed elsewhere" 2>&1 | grep -i "default branch" || echo NO_WARNING

strings: does not verifiably land on the default branch

_note: Asserts the WARNING, not the status: supersede deliberately applies and reports non-verification on stderr rather than refusing. An earlier version asserted the status and would have been testing a behaviour the design never had.
